related_questions.question: How common is a 700 credit score?

text_blocks.snippet: A credit score of 700 is considered "good" and is relatively common, falling within the 670-739 range. While not as high as "very good" or "exceptional" scores, it still indicates a responsible borrower and is likely to result in loan and credit card approvals with potentially favorable terms.
Here's why a 700 credit score is considered good and how common it is:

list.title: Good Credit Score Range:
list.snippet: A 700 credit score falls within the "Good" range of 670-739, according to the FICO® credit scoring model.

list.title: Slightly Below Average:
list.snippet: While it's a good score, it's slightly below the average U.S. credit score, which is generally around 715-717.

list.title: Prevalence:
list.snippet: Approximately 21% of consumers in the U.S. have a credit score in the "Good" range (670-739).

list.title: Positive Implications:
list.snippet: A 700 credit score generally leads to loan and credit card approvals with better interest rates and terms than scores in the "Fair" or "Poor" range.

list.title: Comparison:
list.snippet: While a 700 score is good, scores in the "Very Good" (740-799) or "Exceptional" (800-850) ranges often unlock even more favorable terms from lenders.

related_questions.question: How common is a 750 credit score?

text_blocks.snippet: A credit score of 750 is considered "very good" and is above the average credit score. It's relatively common, with a significant portion of consumers falling within this range. About 48% of consumers have credit scores above 750. Specifically, approximately 24% of consumers fall within the 750-799 range according to The Motley Fool. This score typically qualifies individuals for favorable interest rates and loan terms.

list.title: Good vs. Very Good:
list.snippet: A 750 credit score is on the cusp of "excellent" when using the FICO scoring model, but is considered "very good".

list.title: Commonality:
list.snippet: While a 750 score is above average, it's not as rare as an 800+ score. A large percentage of consumers achieve this level.

list.title: Benefits:
list.snippet: A 750 score generally provides access to lower interest rates, better loan terms, and easier approval for various credit products.

list.title: Room for Improvement:
list.snippet: While 750 is a good score, there's still room for improvement to reach the "excellent" range of 800 and above. Focus on lowering credit utilization, maintaining a mix of credit, and consistent on-time payments.
